title: Welcome to the B2A Economy | Andreessen Horowitz
gist: a16z's Olivia and Justine Moore argue AI agents are becoming the Internet's primary users and the missing distribution leg of AI's platform shift, creating a 'B2A' economy where businesses must compete for agents' business. Evidence includes Shopify's 8x AI traffic / ~13x AI-search orders, 8x agentic browser growth (Muse 60%), and coding-agent spillover to Supabase, Neon, Stripe and Vercel; beneficiaries are agentic models, agent-native products, agent-optimized incumbents and agent infrastructure (payments, fraud, identity).

themes.theme: Agents as the Internet's primary users

insights.claim: a16z's Olivia and Justine Moore claim AI agents now make up the majority of web traffic, write more than half of new articles published online, and generate most code pushed to production.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore and Justine Moore
insights.so_what: If the marginal web 'user' is a bot, traffic, ad and conversion models built on human visitors need re-underwriting.
insights.quote: Agents now make up the majority of web traffic, write more than half of new articles published online, and generate most of the code pushed to production.
insights.locator: Agents now make up the majority

insights.claim: Retailers and platforms that spent years building walls to keep bots out will now have to compete for bots' business; businesses treating agents as first-class customers can capture a growth wave while laggards face threat.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore and Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Anti-bot posture flips from defense to a revenue liability; bot-friendly incumbents gain share.
insights.quote: For years, retailers and platforms built walls to keep bots out. Now they’ll have to fight for bots’ business.

insights.claim: Most enterprises still block agent traffic over fraud and chargeback concerns, but a16z believes they will be forced to embrace it as agent traffic becomes increasingly valuable.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore and Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Fraud/chargeback tooling for agent transactions is the gating unlock — a near-term infrastructure demand signal.
insights.quote: Most enterprises are still blocking agent traffic due to concerns about fraud and chargebacks

insights.claim: As agents shift from answering questions to completing tasks, they will increasingly decide which products to use, which services to subscribe to and where to spend money on users' behalf.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore and Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Purchase decision authority migrates from humans to agents, making agent selection logic the new shelf space.

insights.claim: Every prior platform shift (web, mobile) paired a new product capability with a new distribution mechanism; AI has overperformed on capability but underperformed on distribution, which explains why consumer AI adoption has stayed limited outside ChatGPT.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore and Justine Moore
insights.so_what: The investable gap in consumer AI is distribution, not models — agents as a distribution channel are the 'biggest unrealized opportunity'.
insights.quote: AI has overperformed on the first and underperformed on the second, which is a big reason consumer adoption has stayed so limited outside ChatGPT.

insights.claim: The current agent era resembles the early stage of a platform shift: adoption is measurable but the business models it enables are mostly not yet visible.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore and Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Early-stage positioning window: usage metrics lead monetization, so business-model winners are not yet priced.
insights.quote: adoption is measurable, but the business models it enables mostly aren’t visible yet
insights.locator: This is what the early stage

insights.claim: Just as Amazon needed the Internet and Uber needed the mobile phone, agents should spawn native products — likely self-running SMBs, AI-intermediated marketplaces/network products, and auto-optimizers — though exact form is hard to predict.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore and Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Look for agent-native business models analogous to Amazon/Uber rather than retrofits of existing apps.
insights.quote: Amazon needed the Internet to come to life, and Uber could not have existed without the mobile phone.

insights.claim: Labeling the agent economy 'AI commerce' undersells it: beyond driving transactions for physical goods and services, agents will reshape how traffic, tokens and revenue route to digital products.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore and Justine Moore
insights.so_what: TAM includes digital SaaS signups and token routing, not only e-commerce GMV.
insights.quote: Calling it “AI commerce” undersells the opportunity

themes.theme: Hard data on AI-driven traffic and conversion

insights.claim: Shopify reported AI-driven traffic to its stores grew eightfold year over year in Q1 2026, while orders from AI-powered searches grew nearly thirteenfold.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore and Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Orders growing faster than traffic implies AI referrals carry higher purchase intent — a monetizable channel.
insights.quote: Shopify reported that AI-driven traffic to its stores grew eightfold year over year in Q1 ‘26, while orders from AI-powered searches grew nearly thirteenfold.

insights.claim: Human Security observed agentic browser traffic grow 8x between August and October 2026, with Muse driving the largest share (60%) and OpenAI products a combined 30%.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore and Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Agentic browsing is concentrated in a few harnesses — Muse leads OpenAI in this measure, a non-obvious share signal.
insights.quote: Human Security saw agentic browser traffic grow 8x between August and October, with Muse driving the largest share of activity (60%) and OpenAI products reaching a combined 30%.

insights.claim: AI-referred consumer traffic shows higher engagement, better conversion to revenue and lower bounce rate than non-AI traffic, because agents hold deep, specific data on the user and their needs — making them a stronger referral source than websites, as websites were over billboards.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore and Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Merchants should pay up for agent referrals; referral/affiliate economics shift to agent platforms.
insights.quote: AI-referred consumer traffic is higher engagement and converts better to revenue than non-AI traffic, with a lower bounce rate

insights.claim: Even before agents, an estimated 11% of U.S. shopper journeys visited an AI tool before a transactional site.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore and Justine Moore
insights.so_what: LLMs are already a pre-purchase discovery layer at meaningful scale.
insights.quote: an estimated 11% of shopper journeys in the U.S. visited AI before a transactional site

insights.claim: ChatGPT has 1.2 billion weekly active users, giving it a particularly intriguing opportunity as every product moves to operate agentically.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore and Justine Moore
insights.so_what: ChatGPT's reach positions it as the default agentic distribution platform.
insights.quote: ChatGPT (with 1.2 billion weekly active users) has a particularly intriguing opportunity here.

themes.theme: From browser-use to agent app stores

insights.claim: Most agent traffic today happens via browser use (agents clicking around a user's browser or their own VM), but an 'App Store for agents on steroids' is emerging via connectors, plug-ins and MCPs giving direct access to third-party tools and sites.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore and Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Integration surface shifts from UI scraping to structured APIs; products lacking connectors/MCPs risk being invisible to agents.

insights.claim: In an a16z test, ChatGPT coordinated across Krea, Descript and Eleven Labs plug-ins to create and edit a video ad, and upsold the users on a paid Descript plan to finish the job — evidence agents can drive paid conversions.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore and Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Agents act as salespeople for plug-in partners; being in the agent's toolset drives SaaS upgrades.
insights.quote: It coordinated across the products, and upsold us on a Descript paid plan to get the video done.

insights.claim: Agent-driven signup and payment will get easier as platforms let users 'lend' identity or tokens (e.g., Sign in with ChatGPT); eventually agents will select and install tools without human intervention — Claude already lets enterprise admins connect plugins org-wide, and OpenAI just launched Businesses in ChatGPT for claiming businesses, adding product feeds and viewing interaction insights.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore and Justine Moore
insights.so_what: LLM platforms are building merchant-facing tooling — the analog of Google Business/Shopping for agents.

themes.theme: Who benefits: GEO-to-execution and agent infrastructure

insights.claim: Generative engine optimization (GEO) largely stops at discovery; agents extend optimization into evaluation and execution of purchase/signup choices, which a16z calls an even larger market for incumbents that optimize for agents.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore and Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Next-gen GEO tools covering agent evaluation/checkout are a bigger opportunity than discovery-only GEO.
insights.quote: GEO largely stops at discovery. Agents will take it further, into evaluation and execution of purchase / signup choices, an even larger market.

insights.claim: Systems for payments, fraud and identity, and communication (iMessage, calls, email) are already showing strain at fairly low agent volumes, signaling demand for dedicated agent infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore and Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Agent payments/identity/fraud rails are a near-term bottleneck and investable layer.
insights.quote: We’re already seeing system strain at fairly low agent volume on payments, fraud and identity, and communication (iMessage, calls, email, etc.).

insights.claim: a16z expects every product to soon operate agentically as underlying models become more action-oriented, beyond standalone consumer agent harnesses like Instinct, Muse and Wabi.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore and Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Standalone agent apps may be commoditized as agentic capability becomes a feature everywhere.
insights.quote: We believe every product will soon operate agentically, as the models behind them get more action-oriented.

themes.theme: Coding agents as the leading case study

insights.claim: As of September 2026, upwards of 40% of GitHub PRs started with an agent's draft, versus just 17% six months prior.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore and Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Coding shows how fast agent adoption can flip a workflow — a template for consumer categories.
insights.quote: As of September 2026, upwards of 40% of GitHub PRs started with an agent’s draft – versus just 17% six months prior.

insights.claim: Developer-tool vendors that agents call are seeing outsized growth: Supabase says over 60% of new databases are launched by AI tools (June 2026); Neon says agents deploy 80% of its new databases (May 2025); Stripe says agents drove nearly 40% of documentation traffic and 70% of CLI API-resource requests (June 2026); Vercel says agent-triggered deployments rose 28x in twelve months (October 2026).
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore and Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Picks-and-shovels for agents (the tools agents choose by default) capture growth beyond the agent harnesses themselves.

insights.claim: Fewer than 1% of the global workforce are developers, so if the remaining 99% adopt agents the way developers did, the downstream tool-vendor effect seen in coding could repeat at far larger scale across consumer and business categories.
insights.speaker: Olivia Moore and Justine Moore
insights.so_what: Second-order: expect consumer/SMB analogs of Supabase/Vercel — services agents pick by default — to see similar step-changes.
insights.quote: Fewer than 1% of the global workforce is developers – what happens when the other 99% starts using agents?
